label: Beginner
description: You're at the very start of your swimming journey. The goal right now is building comfort and confidence in the water — not speed or distance.
nextSteps: Sign up for a beginner adult swim class at your local pool
Practice entering the water slowly until it feels familiar
Work on breath control: blowing bubbles under water
Learn to float on your back with an instructor's support

label: Developing Swimmer
tagline: You have the foundation. Now build on it.
description: You can manage yourself in the water and have some basic skills. This is the stage where technique starts to matter — small improvements now lead to big gains later.
nextSteps: Focus on your freestyle arm pull and body rotation
Practice kicking drills with a kickboard
Work on exhaling underwater so you can breathe smoothly
Try swimming two lengths without stopping, then rest

label: Intermediate Swimmer
tagline: Solid skills. Time to add structure.
description: You're a capable swimmer who can handle yourself well in the water. Now it's about endurance, efficiency, and refining strokes so you swim farther with less effort.
nextSteps: Join a masters swim group or structured lap swim session
Learn flip turns to keep your momentum between lengths
Add backstroke or breaststroke to your regular practice
Try interval training: swim, rest, repeat

label: Advanced Swimmer
tagline: You're the real deal. Keep pushing.
description: You swim with confidence and competence across multiple strokes. Your focus now is on performance, consistency, and possibly competitive swimming or open water.
nextSteps: Work with a coach to analyze your stroke on video
Introduce butterfly and individual medley sets
Build a periodized training plan with distance goals
Consider open water swimming or a local swim meet
